subject: Genetics
title: Sexual Selection
description: A short lesson to help you apply Sexual Selection.

hook.text: The peacock's tail is a survival disaster. It's heavy, visible, and slow. But peahens love it—so it persists.

buildup.text: Darwin proposed sexual selection: traits chosen by mates can spread even if they reduce survival chances.

discovery.text: The handicap principle explains it: costly displays prove genetic quality. Only healthy males afford expensive tails.

twist.text: In humans, sexual selection may have driven brain size. Intelligence as a courtship display—a cognitive peacock tail.

climax.text: Sexual selection shows evolution isn't just about surviving. It's about being chosen. Mate preference shapes species.

punchline.text: Evolution doesn't just ask: can you survive? It asks: will anyone choose you?

quiz.question: What is the handicap principle?
options: Females always choose the largest males
